title: docs(adr): ADR-0090 D12 names the organization administrator's assignment boundary; ADR-0131 D3 notes it
body:
Fixes #24135
Clause-②: no

## Summary

Executes the maintainer's ruling of record `6228728551` on #23960 (letter B, 「同意」): the boundary for what an organization administrator may assign is declared in the ADRs first, so the `plugin-security` card (#24136, `Blocked-by:` this one; it remains open) can enforce it.

- **ADR-0090** (`docs/adr/0090-permission-model-v2-concept-convergence.md`): one status-line entry (the ADR's own convention for amendments, beside the 2026-10-15 entry for ruling `6181988435`) and one dated note under D12, `Amended 2026-10-17` — the form D11's 2026-10-14 note uses. D12 now names three kinds of administrator (tenant-level, organization-level, delegated); the organization-level kind creates and removes `sys_user_position` / `sys_user_permission_set` rows for its own organization's members when every distributed set has no wildcard superuser bit, no `adminScope` and only `scope: 'org'` capabilities; `admin_full_access`, platform sets, `organization_admin` itself and every delegated set stay outside; organization-administrator status is conferred by membership grade only. Strict containment and the `everyone` / `guest` anchors are unchanged. Ruling item 4's denylist names the three D10 agent ceilings, which the three conditions mis-settle; the general case behind them is held for the maintainer's decision on #24164. The D12 text above the note is not rewritten.
- **ADR-0131** (`docs/adr/0131-total-organization-ownership-no-null-organization-id.md`): one dated note under D3's assignment paragraph, pointing at the D12 boundary as the rule that sentence runs under. It inherits the denylist by reference.
- No code, no `packages/spec` key, no test, no migration text. The v18 entry's `replacement` text (`18.walled-catalog-tenant-writes-retired`) stays as published.

## Patch round 1 (contract review `6232429140` on head `b0173e29c`, FAIL)

The review found precision 5 of the previous head wrong for this boundary: the three D10 agent ceilings pass the three conditions mechanically but are not wall-bounded on their own. Re-measured here before editing, on `origin/main` `eda6f14b7b`: `mcp_agent_data_read` is `objects: { '*': { allowRead: true } }` with no `rowLevelSecurity` (`default-permission-sets.ts:1427`–`:1435`); the seven SCIM projection objects are `tenantField: null`, `reach: out` in `scripts/platform-object-tenancy-census.json`; `fallbackPermissionSet: null` composes the human baseline to `[]` (`app-default-permission-set.ts:40`–`:57`). The head `61c8a5d34` therefore:

1. moves `mcp_agent_data_read`, `mcp_agent_data_write` and `mcp_agent_restricted` (the last by kind: an agent ceiling is not a person's set) from "Inside" to "Outside (denylist)" in the D12 note's measured paragraph, with the reason — an agent ceiling's bound is the delegating principal's own grants (D10 rule 1), not the organization wall; held by a person as a direct grant, the two reading ceilings carry no row scope on the Layer-0-inert SCIM projection tables, and in a walled deployment with no platform baseline they read every organization's rows there, a read the granting organization administrator does not hold;
2. replaces "names no set at this date" with "names those three sets", keeping the clause that a set shipped later that the conditions cannot settle joins the denylist by an amendment;
3. adds one sentence: the general case — an authored set with a `'*'` read and no row scope on a Layer-0-inert readable object, in a deployment with no platform baseline — is not settled by the note and is held for the maintainer's decision on #24164. No fourth condition is written;
4. tightens "refuses from every non-system writer" to "refuses from every writer": `reserved_identity_position` takes no provenance exemption (`sys-user-position.object.ts:225`–`:265`).

The rule paragraph of the note (the three conditions and the by-name exclusions) is unchanged; the denylist lives in the measured paragraph, as the review prescribed.

## Mechanism assumptions, measured on `origin/main` `eda6f14b7b`

- **A1 — holds.** ADR-0090 keeps amendments as dated `· **Amended** (…)` status-line entries (`:4`–`:8`), and a superseding change also gets a dated blockquote in the decision itself (D11's `> **Amended 2026-10-14 …**`; D3 / D5 / D8 carry `> **Note (2026-10-14) …**`). The 2026-10-15 D12 amendment is status-line only. This PR uses both: the status line, and an `Amended 2026-10-17` blockquote at the end of D12 (D12 now at `:515`).
- **A2 — holds.** ADR-0131 D3's assignment paragraph is `:322`–`:328`. ADR-0131 itself already uses `> **Note (2026-10-14) — …**` blockquotes (`:66`); the note follows that form. No status-line entry was added to ADR-0131: the note changes no D3 text (its inline 2026-10-10 withdrawal at `:315` set the precedent of a note without a status entry).
- **A3 — holds, with the exact fields.** `packages/spec/src/security/capabilities.ts:33` declares `PlatformCapability.scope: 'platform' | 'org'`, and every one of the 10 `PLATFORM_CAPABILITIES` rows sets it (`platform`: `manage_users`, `manage_metadata`, `manage_platform_settings`, `setup.access`, `studio.access`; `org`: `manage_org_users`, `setup.write`, `manage_sharing`, `view_all_audit_log`, `manage_mailboxes`). A package capability declares it through `CapabilityDeclarationSchema.scope` (`:189`), `z.enum(['platform', 'org']).default('platform')`. The superuser bits are `ObjectPermissionSchema.viewAllRecords` / `modifyAllRecords` on the `objects['*']` entry; the delegation key is `PermissionSetSchema.adminScope` (`permission.zod.ts:1022`). All three conditions are readable from declarations alone.
- **A4 — measured; the conditions settle five of the eight shipped sets, and ruling item 4's denylist names the other three (the D10 agent ceilings).** Table below. The shipped roster is the eight sets in `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/objects/default-permission-sets.ts`, held equal to `SHIPPED_PERMISSION_SET_NAMES` (`packages/cli/src/utils/organization-ownership-inventory.ts:215`) by that file's test; a repo-wide search for `PermissionSetSchema.parse(` / `definePermissionSet(` outside tests finds no other shipped set (fixtures in `packages/verify` and `packages/qa` only).
- **A5 — holds.** No heading was added (both notes are blockquotes), so no anchor moved; `pnpm check:adr-anchors` exits 0 on the final head.

### Shipped permission sets against the three conditions

| set | (a) no `*` superuser bit | (b) no `adminScope` | (c) `org` capabilities only | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `admin_full_access` | no — `viewAllRecords` + `modifyAllRecords` | yes | no — `manage_users`, `manage_metadata`, `manage_platform_settings`, `setup.access`, `studio.access` | **outside** |
| `organization_admin` | no — `viewAllRecords` + `modifyAllRecords` | yes | no — `setup.access` | **outside** (also by name) |
| `organization_admin_no_bypass` | yes — the derivation drops both bits | yes | no — `setup.access` | **outside** (also by name) |
| `member_default` | yes — no `*` entry at all | yes | yes — none | inside |
| `viewer_readonly` | yes — `allowRead` only | yes | yes — none | inside (it carries the SCIM row scope itself) |
| `mcp_agent_data_read` | yes — `allowRead` only, no row scope | yes | yes — none | **outside (denylist)** — mis-settled |
| `mcp_agent_data_write` | yes — CRUD bits only, no row scope | yes | yes — none | **outside (denylist)** — mis-settled |
| `mcp_agent_restricted` | yes — `objects: {}` | yes | yes — none | **outside (denylist)** — by kind |

Shipped positions: the four ADR-0068 D2 identity names (`platform_admin`, `org_owner`, `org_admin`, `org_member`) are refused on `sys_user_position.position` for every writer by the object validation `reserved_identity_position` (`sys-user-position.object.ts:256`, no provenance exemption), and the two anchors by the gate's unconditional anchor refusal (`delegated-admin-gate.ts:298`–`:312`). Neither is a question for this boundary; the note records them as unchanged.

## Precisions the contract review should read

Each narrows; none widens the ruled rule.

1. **"Tenant-level" is the platform administrator alone.** ADR-0095 names the organization administrator's posture rung `TENANT_ADMIN`; the note says in so many words that D12's "tenant-level" is the first kind only, so the two vocabularies cannot be read into each other.
2. **Condition (c) is fail-closed on an undeclared scope.** A package declaration that omits `scope` defaults to `'platform'`, and a `systemPermissions` name no declaration carries is not an `org` capability.
3. **"Each set a position carries" includes the position-name fold.** The resolver requests `[...positions, ...explicitPermissionSets]` (`security-plugin.ts:6542`), so a held position also grants the permission set of its own name; the note counts that set while the fold stands. Without this a position could carry an outside set past the boundary.
4. **Both organization-administrator variants are outside by name.** `organization_admin_no_bypass` is outside by (c) today only because `setup.access` is `platform`; the note also excludes it by name, which is what "conferred by membership grade only" requires.
5. **The three D10 agent ceilings are outside, on ruling item 4's denylist.** The conditions place them inside and so mis-settle them: an agent ceiling's bound is the delegating principal's own grants (D10 rule 1), not the organization wall. Held by a person as a direct grant there is no intersection, and the two reading ceilings carry no row scope on the seven Layer-0-inert SCIM projection tables; in a walled deployment with no platform baseline (`fallbackPermissionSet: null`) they read every organization's rows there, a read the granting organization administrator does not hold (its explicit per-object entries keep the `_self` / `_none` scope). `mcp_agent_restricted` is named by kind. The general case — any authored set with a `'*'` read and no row scope on a Layer-0-inert readable object, in a no-baseline deployment — is not settled by the conditions or by a shipped-set denylist; the note holds it for the maintainer's decision on #24164 and writes no fourth condition.
6. **Create and remove only** — the ruling's `allowCreate` / `allowDelete` on, `allowEdit` off.

- `node scripts/check-adr-symbol-anchors.mjs` :: exit 0 — "2353 anchors across 142 records resolve"; `--self-test` :: exit 0

`--ran` reconciliation: "19 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 19 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED (a DERIVED zero — all 19 recorded an exit code and none of them is 3)".

`node scripts/pm/check-governed-merges.mjs --branch claude/issue-24135-adr-0090-d12-org-admin-boundary` (exit 3, the governed code): "GOVERNED — a human merge is the review record for this PR", "landing tier: H(人合)", `docs/adr/**` ×2, under the 3000-line threshold.

Everything else CI runs on this PR is CI's; nothing was re-run locally. No package builds or tests are owed: the diff touches no package.

## Acceptance notes

Read-only inferences from the measurement above, not reproduced and not filed:

- The delegated gate's position walk (`setsBoundToPosition`, `delegated-admin-gate.ts:1086`) reads only the definition's `permissionSets`, while the resolver also grants the set of the position's own name (precision 3). A delegate's allowlist check therefore does not see a same-named set. Carrier: #24136, whose third branch reuses that walk.
- `isTenantAdmin` (`delegated-admin-gate.ts:256`, a wildcard `modifyAllRecords` holder) reads the walled `organization_admin` as tenant-level and the wall-less variant as no administrator at all; under the amended D12 both are organization-level. Carrier: #24136.
- The companion reference `docs/design/permission-model.md` §10 describes delegated administration only; the organization-level kind belongs there once #24136 enforces it (docs follow the implementation). Carrier: #24136.
- The D10 agent ceilings as a person's direct grant: the shipped instance is now on the item-4 denylist in this PR (precision 5); the general class — an authored wildcard-read set with no row scope on a Layer-0-inert object, in a no-baseline deployment — is the maintainer's decision on #24164, filed by the seat.

## 维护者速读(草稿)

### 改了什么

在权限模型 ADR-0090 的 D12(管理权限)里加了一条带日期的修订,并在 ADR-0131 D3 下加了一行注记,纯文字,不改代码、不加 spec 键。修订把管理者分成三类:租户级(平台管理员)、组织级(组织的 owner / admin,自动获得组织管理员权限集)、委托级(带 `adminScope` 的人)。组织级管理员可以给**本组织成员**增加或移除岗位与权限集,但只限"被组织墙约束住"的集:不带通配超级用户位、不带 `adminScope`、所含能力全部是组织级。`admin_full_access`、平台级集、组织管理员集本身、任何委托集都不能分;组织管理员身份只能由成员资格(owner / admin)获得,不能靠分配复制。本轮按席位复核意见补了一条:三个给 AI 代理用的 MCP 上限权限集列入裁决预留的黑名单,组织管理员不能把它们分给人。

### 为什么改

这是您 10 月 17 日对 #23960 的裁决 B(「同意」)的第一步。ADR-0131 D3 承诺"组织的管理员给本组织成员分配",但代码为了防止组织管理员给自己绑 `admin_full_access` 越过组织墙,把两张分配表设成了只读;缺的正是"组织管理员能分配哪些"这条边界。边界先写进 ADR,代码卡 #24136(被本卡阻塞)才能开工。实测出货的 8 个权限集:三条件能判定 5 个(2 个在内、3 个在外);剩下 3 个 MCP 代理上限集按三条件看似在内,但它们本来只配给 AI 代理、靠委托人自己的权限收窄,直接分给人时在"不配平台基线"的部署里能读到其他组织的 SCIM 身份数据,而分配它的组织管理员自己都读不到——所以按裁决第 4 条列入黑名单。

### 风险与代价(含回滚)

只改两份 ADR 的文字,今天的产品行为不变:两张分配表仍然只读,直到 #24136 落地。规则措辞上的几处精确化全部是收紧、没有放宽:未声明范围的能力按平台级算;岗位按名字带出的同名权限集也算"岗位携带的集";无墙部署用的 `organization_admin_no_bypass` 也按名字排除;三个 MCP 上限集列入黑名单。还有一个更一般的口子没有在本 ADR 里定:任何自建的"通配只读、没有行级范围"的权限集,在不配平台基线的部署里同样能碰到那几张没有组织列的 SCIM 表——是否加第四个条件,还是把保证写成"以平台基线为前提",已单独立成待您决策的 #24164,本 PR 不替您决定。回滚:直接 revert 本 PR,不涉及数据和发布。

### 席位意见

### 你要做的(一个动作)

席位复核通过后,在本 PR 上点 Approve。
